## Taxonomic scope

VirMarkDB currently covers three viral groups, each targeted through a different marker gene. Taxonomy is derived from the ICTV Virus Metadata Resource [VMR_MSL41.v1.20260320](https://ictv.global/sites/default/files/VMR/VMR_MSL41.v1.20260320.xlsx).

[![](assets/ictv_logo.png)](https://ictv.global/)

| Group | Kingdom | Phylum (scope) | Genomes | Families | Marker gene(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Giant viruses | Bamfordvirae | Nucleocytoviricota | 224 | 15 | `atpase`, `dnapol`, `majorcapsid`, `primase`, `rnapol1`, `rnapol2`, `tf2s`, `vltf3` |
| Phages | Heunggongvirae | Pantevenvirales | 431 | 9 | `g23` |
| RNA viruses | Orthornavirae | Lenarviricota, Pisuviricota, Kitrinoviricota, Negarnaviricota, Duplornaviricota | 7,950 | 137 | `rdrp` |

Taxonomy from Kingdom to Species is derived from the ICTV VMR. Manually added genomes follow the same taxonomy fields. See [Workflow → Additional genome inputs](workflow.qmd#additional-genome-inputs) for how these are incorporated.

## Marker genes

Ten conserved marker genes are targeted across the three groups.

### Giant viruses (*Nucleocytoviricota*)

| Marker | Description |
|---|---|
| `majorcapsid` | Major capsid protein (MCP) |
| `dnapol` | DNA polymerase B |
| `atpase` | Packaging ATPase |
| `primase` | Primase |
| `rnapol1` | RNA polymerase subunit 1 |
| `rnapol2` | RNA polymerase subunit 2 |
| `tf2s` | Transcription factor S-II / TFIIS-like |
| `vltf3` | Viral late transcription factor 3 |

### Phages (*Pantevenvirales*)

| Marker | Description |
|---|---|
| `g23` | Major capsid protein gp23 |

### RNA viruses (*Orthornavirae*)

| Marker | Description |
|---|---|
| `rdrp` | RNA-dependent RNA polymerase |

## Why marker groups exist

Some marker genes are too divergent across viral lineages to be represented by a single HMM profile. VirMarkDB solves this with **marker groups**: each one ties together a marker gene, a taxonomic scope, a reference protein set, and a dedicated HMM profile built from that set. This keeps a common marker-gene framework across the database while letting each lineage be represented by a profile calibrated on its own reference sequences.

::: {.callout-note}
This page describes the *concept*. The mechanics (how `mapfile.tsv` encodes marker groups and drives the pipeline) are covered once, in [Workflow → Marker-group configuration](workflow.qmd#marker-group-configuration).
:::

## Where the data lives

Released sequences, metadata tables, and per-ORF tables are distributed as a versioned archive. For the exact directory layout, FASTA header syntax, and TSV column definitions, see [Files & formats](files-formats.qmd).

For genome and marker coverage numbers, see [Analyses](analysis.qmd).
